decision.sql:
WITH lf_orders AS (
  SELECT
    o.customer_id,
    o.business_date,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.customer_id ORDER BY o.business_date) AS rn,
    LAG(o.business_date) OVER (PARTITION BY o.customer_id ORDER BY o.business_date) AS prev_date
  FROM orders o
  WHERE o.business_line = 'laundry_farm'
),
gaps AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    business_date,
    prev_date,
    julianday(business_date) - julianday(prev_date) AS gap_days
  FROM lf_orders
  WHERE prev_date IS NOT NULL
),
weekly_gaps_per_customer AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    COUNT(*) AS weekly_gap_count
  FROM gaps
  WHERE gap_days BETWEEN 5 AND 9
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
last_order AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    MAX(business_date) AS last_order_date
  FROM orders
  WHERE business_line = 'laundry_farm'
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
qualified AS (
  SELECT
    w.customer_id,
    w.weekly_gap_count,
    l.last_order_date
  FROM weekly_gaps_per_customer w
  JOIN last_order l ON l.customer_id = w.customer_id
  WHERE w.weekly_gap_count >= 4
    AND julianday('2026-10-14') - julianday(l.last_order_date) > 30
)
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  c.name,
  c.paid_orders,
  c.lifetime_cents,
  c.first_order_date,
  q.last_order_date,
  q.weekly_gap_count,
  CAST(julianday('2026-10-14') - julianday(q.last_order_date) AS INTEGER) AS days_since_last_order
FROM qualified q
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = q.customer_id
ORDER BY q.weekly_gap_count DESC, days_since_last_order DESC
LIMIT 100

decision.answer: These Laundry Farm customers each had at least 4 consecutive order gaps of 5–9 days (a weekly cadence) but have placed no recorded paid order in the last 107 days. Their weekly habit appears to have broken around late June 2026. All 10 qualify as lapsed regulars worth re-engagement outreach.

decision.sql:
WITH customer_orders AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    order_month,
    COUNT(*) AS monthly_orders,
    SUM(amount_cents) AS monthly_cents
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY customer_id, order_month
),
customer_activity AS (
  SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    c.name,
    c.paid_orders,
    c.lifetime_cents,
    c.first_order_date,
    c.last_order_date,
    c.has_contact,
    c.identity_matched,
    c.neighborhoods,
    -- months active (distinct months with orders)
    (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_month) FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id) AS active_months,
    -- days since last order
    CAST(julianday('2026-10-14') - julianday(c.last_order_date) AS INTEGER) AS days_since_last,
    -- avg days between orders (window span / gaps)
    CASE WHEN c.paid_orders > 1 THEN
      CAST((julianday(c.last_order_date) - julianday(c.first_order_date)) / (c.paid_orders - 1) AS INTEGER)
    ELSE NULL END AS avg_days_between_orders
  FROM customers c
  WHERE c.paid_orders >= 3
    AND c.identity_matched = 1
),
segmented AS (
  SELECT *,
    CASE
      WHEN days_since_last <= 60 THEN 'active'
      WHEN days_since_last <= 180 THEN 'at_risk'
      WHEN days_since_last <= 365 THEN 'lapsed'
      ELSE 'dormant'
    END AS recency_segment,
    CASE
      WHEN avg_days_between_orders IS NOT NULL AND avg_days_between_orders <= 30 THEN 'high_freq'
      WHEN avg_days_between_orders IS NOT NULL AND avg_days_between_orders <= 90 THEN 'mid_freq'
      ELSE 'low_freq'
    END AS freq_segment
  FROM customer_activity
)
SELECT
  recency_segment,
  freq_segment,
  COUNT(*) AS customers,
  SUM(CASE WHEN has_contact = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS with_contact,
  SUM(CASE WHEN has_contact = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS no_contact,
  ROUND(AVG(paid_orders), 1) AS avg_orders,
  ROUND(AVG(lifetime_cents) / 100.0, 2) AS avg_lifetime_dollars,
  ROUND(AVG(days_since_last), 0) AS avg_days_since_last,
  ROUND(AVG(avg_days_between_orders), 0) AS avg_cadence_days,
  ROUND(AVG(active_months), 1) AS avg_active_months
FROM segmented
GROUP BY recency_segment, freq_segment
ORDER BY
  CASE recency_segment WHEN 'active' THEN 1 WHEN 'at_risk' THEN 2 WHEN 'lapsed' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END,
  CASE freq_segment WHEN 'high_freq' THEN 1 WHEN 'mid_freq' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END

decision.answer: Recurring identity-matched customers (3+ orders) split into just two segments. The at-risk high-frequency group is the primary recovery target: frequent buyers (~9-day cadence) who have gone quiet for ~100 days — all have contact info, making outreach feasible. The two active high-frequency customers show healthy engagement. Missing evidence: costs (no margin view), CleanCloud open orders (some "lapsed" customers may have outstanding orders), and the broader lapsed/dormant population is absent from this cohort, suggesting most multi-order customers are either unmatched identities or below the 3-order threshold — a data-quality gap that limits recovery targeting.
